summary: Runaway batching cascade: mitigation and tenant demote checklist
description:
Issue summary: BrightPost reports a dramatic throughput inversion and sustained tail-latency increase after a staged optimizer push that enabled aggressive continuous batching + KV-prefetch for their tenant. Impact: Several routes for the tenant returned >95th percentile latency spikes (2000-3500 ms) and a sustained decrease in successful QPS despite increased offered load; customer-facing outages for low-latency endpoints were observed for ~45 minutes. They requested immediate guidance to mitigate and a safe stepwise demote plan that preserves session continuity for long-lived conversations.

Environment: Dedicated pool (d-prod-e5), tenant: brightpost-prod, model: redwood/open-7b-v2 pinned at v2026-03-08-optA. Autoscaling policy: aggressive-cpu-driven with continuous-batching enabled and kv-prefetch=true.

Customer request: 1) Immediate mitigation to restore latency SLOs. 2) A low-risk rollback/demote checklist that can be executed during business hours without data loss. 3) Post-incident recommendations to avoid recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy optimizer profile 'optA' to tenant brightpost-prod with continuous_batching=enabled, max_batch_size=256, kv_prefetch=true, quant_profile=dynamic-int8.
2) Ramp traffic in a canary-to-100% pattern over 15 minutes using steady arrived RPS (customer traffic pattern includes many long chat sessions with tokens per session >1000).
3) Observe scheduler increasing batch aggregation window to maintain throughput; KV-prefetch begins preloading large prefix caches leading to memory pressure and eviction churn.
4) Observe token latency tail rising and overall successful QPS dropping as requests are retried or timed out downstream.
logs: 2026-03-10T13:45:12Z api-gateway ERROR route=/v1/chat generate 504 downstream_timeout latency_ms=3120
comments: BrightPost Support (2026-03-10 13:48) - 'We started seeing errors and slow responses around 13:35 UTC after the optimizer rollout. Can you roll back to yesterday's behavior? Production impact is ongoing.'
Support (Aisha) (2026-03-10 13:52) - 'Acknowledged. We're triaging. Please keep traffic steady and do not retry bursts. Can you share the last snapshot id from your console snapshot feed?'

SRE (Tom) (2026-03-10 13:58) - 'Initial hypothesis: continuous batching has widened aggregation windows under this workload pattern, and kv-prefetch is causing aggressive memory usage and eviction churn which in turn increases disk/ram I/O. Will attempt a per-tenant throttle and staged demote.'
BrightPost (2026-03-10 14:05) - 'Snapshot id s-2026-03-09-brightpost-001 attached in console. We need a plan that keeps long chat sessions intact.'
Support (Tom) (2026-03-10 14:12) - 'Applying temporary per-tenant max_batch_size=64 and disabling kv-prefetch for brightpost-prod now. Will monitor for 10 minutes then recommend next steps.'
investigation_notes: Telemetry shows avg_batch_size jumped from ~24 to ~187 in the 8-minute window after optA rollout. The scheduler's adaptive window increased due to sudden per-tenant token arrival variance.
KV cache metrics: thrash rate increased by 7x; resident set exceeded expected footprint causing host memory_pressure>0.8 and swap activity on some nodes.

Quant_profile dynamic-int8 did not show immediate accuracy regressions on sampled outputs, but may increase model memory footprints in this implementation causing additional GC pressure in the serving runtime.
Confirmed that disabling kv-prefetch and constraining batch size reduces tail latency rapidly in a controlled pilot for 5% shadow traffic.
resolution_notes: Mitigation executed (2026-03-10 14:15): Applied per-tenant overrides: continuous_batching=enabled, max_batch_size=64, kv_prefetch=false, batch_wait_ms_target=40. Immediate effect: 95p latency dropped from ~2600ms to ~420ms within three minutes for the pilot group.

Demote plan executed (staged, 2026-03-10 14:30-15:00): Step 1: Create optimizer snapshot of current optA (snapshot id s-2026-03-10-optA). Step 2: Roll traffic to optA-light profile for 25% traffic for 10 minutes (optA-light = continuous_batching=enabled, max_batch_size=48, kv_prefetch=false, quant_profile=static-int8). Step 3: If metrics stabilise, expand to 60% then 100% over 10-minute windows. We followed this staged plan and reached 100% at 15:00 UTC with stable latencies and restored QPS.
Communication: Notified BrightPost via support channel at each step; scheduled post-mortem and follow-up engineering review to harden gating.

Permanent action: Created follow-up PR to implement a per-tenant batching circuit-breaker (see PR #7123) and added conservative defaults for kv-prefetch on dedicated tenants with long-session profiles.
follow_up_actions: 1) Engineering to add a telemetry-derived soft-circuit-breaker that auto-bounds max_batch_size when kv_cache_evictions > threshold for 60s.

2) Product to update optimizer rollout checklist to require a tenant profile classification (long-session vs short-session) and to default kv_prefetch=false for long-session tenants unless explicitly validated.
3) Support to create a tenant-level alerting playbook that surfaces 'batch_size inversion' and recommends immediate per-tenant override commands.
4) Schedule a 2026-03-14 post-incident review with BrightPost and Engineering to validate changes and capture action owners.
